homes.body: Bellevue is where we are based, and it is a city of very mixed housing. Nearly half of its single-family homes were built between 1960 and 1979, so many are now ready for new kitchens, bathrooms, roofs and systems, while newer plats need finishing work, decks and outdoor space. The western lakeside pockets of Enatai, Beaux Arts and Meydenbauer hold architect-designed mid-century houses with post-and-beam framing and low-slope roofs. homes.body: Normandy Park was planned as something distinctive. In the 1920s the Seattle-Tacoma Land Company platted about 1,200 acres of Puget Sound shoreline between Des Moines and Burien, laying out winding roads and a water system around a French Normandy architectural theme. The Depression halted the project, and the area was not really built out until it was rediscovered in the late 1940s and early 1950s, with the city incorporating in 1953. The result is a quiet, green community where roughly three quarters of the city is zoned for single-family lots of 15,000 square feet or larger, and tree canopy covers close to half of Normandy Park, among the highest shares in King County. Homes range from mid-century houses to newer custom builds, many set among mature trees on generous lots, some with water views. Because of that range and the wooded shoreline setting, we start every project with a careful look at the house and lot you already have, planning for roofs, drainage and exterior exposure alongside the finishes.

Rust built a smelter and a company town on Commencement Bay, and residents voted to name the place Ruston in his honor in 1906. Many of the homes near the original town center date to that company-town era, while the former smelter site has been redeveloped as Point Ruston, a waterfront district of newer condos, shops and a waterwalk. homes.body: Yarrow Point is a small, affluent town on a peninsula that reaches about a mile north into Lake Washington, forming the west shore of Yarrow Bay just south of Kirkland, and home remodeling in Yarrow Point is almost entirely residential work on custom houses. One of the three Points communities alongside Hunts Point and Evergreen Point, the town covers roughly 231 acres with about 405 homes. It was first homesteaded in the late 1880s and incorporated in 1959 to protect its character, taking its name from newspaper publisher Leigh Hunt, who called it after the yarrow flower native to the area. About a quarter of the homes sit on the waterfront or have water access, and most of the rest hold views ranging from territorial to expansive. Because so many lots touch or overlook the lake, careful moisture protection and shoreline review shape the work. We plan each project around the individual house.

faqs.a: The finishes should match the rest of a custom home, built on sound waterproofing and ventilation that handle the wet climate. We size a walk-in shower or soaking tub to the room and keep the work tidy on a close-knit street.

faqs.a: Yes. About a quarter of homes here are on the water, and work near the shoreline can involve shoreline or critical-area review through the Town of Yarrow Point. We confirm what applies and plan moisture protection and drainage accordingly.
